newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-ELLIOTT TO MISS THIRD TEST AFTER SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ELLIOTT TO MISS THIRD TEST AFTER SURGERY.

text.p: A knee injury suffered by Australia batsman Matthew Elliott this week was more serious than first thought and the young left-hander will be out of cricket for over a month, his manager said on Wednesday.
Elliott underwent surgery on Tuesday to repair cartilage damage in his right knee after colliding with batting partner Mark Waugh during the second test against West Indies on Monday.
The 25-year-old had hoped to be fit for the third test starting in Melbourne on December 26 but is now unlikely to be fit before the fourth test in Adelaide starting on January 25.

"Matthew will be on crutches for four weeks and hopes to return to cricket and prove his fitness in time to be available for selection for the Adelaide test," Elliott's manager Rob Aivatoglou said in a statement.
Aivatoglou said surgeon David Young expected Elliott to make a full recovery.
Elliott topped the Australian domestic averages last season and made his international debut in the first test in Brisbane.

Chosen to replace discarded opener Michael Slater, Elliott made a duck in the first innings in Brisbane but had moved confidently to 78 not out in the second innings in Sydney and appeared set for his maiden test century before he was forced to retire hurt after colliding with Waugh.
Australia beat West Indies by 124 runs in the second test to take a 2-0 lead in the five-test series.
